title: A vector bundle stalk inverse extends to an open neighbourhood
statement: Let $W$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $M,N$ be finite locally free $\mathcal O_W$-modules [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf], let $\varphi:M\to N$, and let $x\in W$. If the stalk map $\varphi_x$ [def-pc-module-stalk-functor] is an isomorphism, then there exists an open $U\subseteq W$ containing $x$ such that the tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] of $\varphi$ along the open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] $U\hookrightarrow W$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 10.79.2, label lemma-map-between-finitely-presented, finite inverse extension; also Tag 00O0(3)

proof.text: Extend the inverse of the module-stalk map to a morphism on a neighbourhood U. Its two composites with the restricted original map equal the identity on germs, by the two inverse identities of the stalk isomorphism.

Apply the shrinking equality theorem to both composites, using finite local freeness of M and N respectively. Intersect the two resulting neighbourhoods. Restriction composition transports both equalities to this common open and gives a two-sided inverse.
Compare restriction and tensor pullback using uniqueness of left adjoints to pushforward. Naturality transports the resulting isomorphism to tensorPullback.

proof_origin.place: T3 Lean proof: extend the stalk inverse, shrink its two inverse identities, and compare left adjoints.

theorem exists_isIso_tensorPullback_of_isIso_moduleStalkMap
    {W : Scheme.{u}} (M N : W.Modules)
    [M.IsFiniteLocallyFree] [N.IsFiniteLocallyFree] (φ : M ⟶ N) (x : W)
    (hφ : IsIso ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor W.toRingedSpace x).map φ)) :
    ∃ U : W.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ IsIso ((tensorPullback U.ι).map φ)
